category: PyAEDT: 3D Modeler Primitives, Booleans, Coordinate Systems & CAD
description: The Modeler3D object (hfss.modeler) beyond the basic box/cylinder calls: every primitive (cones, circles, ellipses, tori, helices, spirals, coax and waveguide builders, bondwires, equation curves, UDPs), the polyline segment types, coordinate systems, air regions, all boolean and transform operations, sheet/solid conversions, face and object lists, geometry queries, 3D components, mesh (Nastran/STL) and CAD import, healing and export. Numbers are in the model units; strings may carry units or variable expressions.

tools.name: hfss.modeler.create_cone
tools.description: Create a truncated cone (or a full cone when the top radius is zero) from the centre of its base, the two radii and the height along the chosen axis. Used for horn antenna flares, conical monopoles, tapered coax transitions and radome tips; the returned Object3d handle carries faces and edges for later port or boundary assignment.
tools.usage:
obj = hfss.modeler.create_cone(orientation=None, origin=None, bottom_radius=None, top_radius=None,
                               height=None, name=None, material=None, **kwargs)

parameters.name: orientation
parameters.description: Axis of the cone: "X", "Y", "Z" or the Axis enum; None means Z.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: [x, y, z] centre of the bottom face.

parameters.name: bottom_radius / top_radius
parameters.description: Radii in model units or unit strings; top_radius=0 gives a pointed cone.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Height along the orientation axis; negative values grow in the opposite direction.

parameters.name: name / material
parameters.description: Object name and material; defaults are assigned when omitted.

tools.example:
flare = hfss.modeler.create_cone(orientation="Z", origin=[0, 0, 20], bottom_radius="a_wg",
                                 top_radius="a_wg*2.5", height="40mm", name="Flare", material="vacuum")
hfss.assign_finite_conductivity(flare.faces[0].id, "aluminum")   # wall face
tools.notes: Native: oEditor.CreateCone(["NAME:ConeParameters", "XCenter:=", ..., "WhichAxis:=", "Z", "Height:=", ..., "BottomRadius:=", ..., "TopRadius:=", ...], ["NAME:Attributes", ...]). A cone with equal radii is a cylinder; use create_cylinder for that.

tools.name: hfss.modeler.create_circle
tools.description: Draw a circular sheet (covered) or a circular line (uncovered) in a coordinate plane. Circle sheets are the usual port faces of coaxial lines, the base of PML/absorber caps and the sheets for lumped RLC or impedance boundaries; num_sides turns the true circle into a regular polygon for meshing control or for matching faceted CAD.
tools.usage:
obj = hfss.modeler.create_circle(orientation, origin, radius, num_sides=0, is_covered=True,
                                 name=None, material=None, non_model=False, **kwargs)

parameters.name: orientation
parameters.description: Plane of the circle: "XY", "YZ", "ZX" (or Plane enum); the normal is the third axis.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: [x, y, z] centre.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: Radius, number or unit/expression string.

parameters.name: num_sides
parameters.description: 0 = true circle, otherwise number of polygon sides.

parameters.name: is_covered
parameters.description: True creates a sheet, False a closed polyline.

parameters.name: non_model
parameters.description: True creates a non-model object (visible, not solved).

tools.example:
port_sheet = hfss.modeler.create_circle("YZ", ["-coax_len", 0, 0], "r_outer", name="CoaxPort")
hfss.wave_port(port_sheet.name, integration_line=[["-coax_len", "r_inner", 0], ["-coax_len", "r_outer", 0]],
               impedance=50, name="P1")
tools.notes: Native: oEditor.CreateCircle(["NAME:CircleParameters", "IsCovered:=", True, "XCenter:=", ..., "Radius:=", ..., "WhichAxis:=", "X", "NumSegments:=", "0"], attrs). A sheet used as a wave port must lie on the outer surface of the model or on a PEC-backed cap.

tools.name: hfss.modeler.create_ellipse
tools.description: Draw an elliptical sheet or closed line from its centre, major radius and the ratio of minor to major radius. Elliptical waveguide ports, elliptical patch antennas and elliptical apertures are built directly instead of scaling a circle, which would also scale the object's history.
tools.usage:
obj = hfss.modeler.create_ellipse(orientation, origin, major_radius, ratio, is_covered=True,
                                  name=None, material=None, segments=0, **kwargs)

parameters.name: orientation
parameters.description: Coordinate plane, "XY"/"YZ"/"ZX".

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: [x, y, z] centre.

parameters.name: major_radius
parameters.description: Radius along the first axis of the plane.

parameters.name: ratio
parameters.description: minor/major radius ratio (0 < ratio <= 1).

parameters.name: segments
parameters.description: 0 for a true ellipse, or number of straight segments.

tools.example:
ell = hfss.modeler.create_ellipse("XY", [0, 0, "h"], "20mm", 0.6, name="EllPatch", material="copper")
hfss.assign_perfecte_to_sheets(ell.name)
tools.notes: Native: oEditor.CreateEllipse(["NAME:EllipseParameters", "IsCovered:=", True, "XCenter:=", ..., "MajRadius:=", ..., "Ratio:=", ..., "WhichAxis:=", "Z", "NumSegments:=", "0"], attrs).

tools.name: hfss.modeler.create_torus
tools.description: Create a torus from its centre, major (ring) radius, minor (tube) radius and axis of revolution. Toroidal inductors and chokes, ring resonators and rounded edges are modelled with it; the minor radius must be smaller than the major radius to keep the solid valid.
tools.usage: obj = hfss.modeler.create_torus(origin, major_radius, minor_radius, axis=None, name=None, material=None, **kwargs)

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: [x, y, z] centre of the ring.

parameters.name: major_radius
parameters.description: Distance from the centre to the tube axis.

parameters.name: minor_radius
parameters.description: Tube radius (must be < major_radius).

parameters.name: axis
parameters.description: "X", "Y" or "Z" axis of revolution; None = Z.

tools.example: core = hfss.modeler.create_torus([0, 0, 0], "12mm", "3mm", axis="Z", name="FerriteCore", material="ferrite")
tools.notes: Native: oEditor.CreateTorus(["NAME:TorusParameters", "XCenter:=", ..., "MajorRadius:=", ..., "MinorRadius:=", ..., "WhichAxis:=", "Z"], attrs). Ferrite materials in HFSS need a Magnetic Bias excitation to be modelled as gyrotropic.

tools.name: hfss.modeler.create_helix
tools.description: Sweep an existing profile polyline into a helix, the modeler's Draw > Helix operation. The profile (usually a small circle or a rectangle cross-section polyline) is revolved around an axis through the origin while advancing by the start-direction vector per turn, optionally with a radius increment for conical helices. This is how helical antennas, springs and coil inductors are built.
tools.usage:
obj = hfss.modeler.create_helix(assignment, origin, x_start_dir, y_start_dir, z_start_dir,
                                turns=1, right_hand=True, radius_increment=0.0, thread=1, **kwargs)

parameters.name: assignment
parameters.description: Name of the polyline (profile) to sweep.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: [x, y, z] point on the helix axis.

parameters.name: x_start_dir / y_start_dir / z_start_dir
parameters.description: Vector giving the axis direction and the pitch (advance per turn).

parameters.name: turns
parameters.description: Number of turns.

parameters.name: right_hand
parameters.description: Handedness of the winding.

parameters.name: radius_increment
parameters.description: Radial change per turn; non-zero makes a conical helix.

tools.example:
prof = hfss.modeler.create_circle("XY", ["r_helix", 0, 0], "wire_r", name="WireProfile")
helix = hfss.modeler.create_helix(prof.name, origin=[0, 0, 0], x_start_dir=0, y_start_dir=0,
                                  z_start_dir="pitch", turns=6, right_hand=True)
helix.material_name = "copper"
tools.notes: Native: oEditor.CreateHelix(["NAME:Selections", "Selections:=", "WireProfile", ...], ["NAME:HelixParameters", "CoordinateSystemID:=", -1, "StartHelixPointX:=", ..., "RadiusChange:=", ..., "NumThread:=", 1, "RightHanded:=", True, "Turns:=", 6]). The profile must lie in a plane containing the axis for a clean sweep.

tools.name: hfss.modeler.create_spiral
tools.description: Generate a planar spiral inductor as a polyline with rectangular cross-section: polygonal turns (default octagonal) starting at an inner radius with a given spacing, conductor width and thickness. It returns the Polyline object so the trace can be extended with feed segments, and is the quickest way to get an on-chip or PCB spiral into an HFSS design.
tools.usage:
poly = hfss.modeler.create_spiral(internal_radius=10, spacing=1, faces=8, turns=10, width=2,
                                  thickness=1, elevation=0, material="copper", name=None, **kwargs)

parameters.name: internal_radius
parameters.description: Radius of the innermost turn.

parameters.name: spacing
parameters.description: Gap between turns (pitch minus width).

parameters.name: faces
parameters.description: Number of sides per turn (4 = square, 8 = octagonal spiral).

parameters.name: turns
parameters.description: Number of turns.

parameters.name: width / thickness
parameters.description: Trace width and metal thickness of the rectangular cross-section.

parameters.name: elevation
parameters.description: Z position of the spiral plane.

tools.example:
spiral = hfss.modeler.create_spiral(internal_radius=60, spacing=8, faces=8, turns=3.5,
                                    width=10, thickness=2, elevation="h_ox", material="copper", name="L1")
print(spiral.name, len(spiral.points))
tools.notes: Units are the modeler units (set hfss.modeler.model_units = "um" first for IC spirals). For multi-layer spirals with underpass, draw the underpass separately and unite through a via box.

tools.name: hfss.modeler.create_coaxial
tools.description: Build a complete coaxial line - inner conductor, dielectric and outer conductor as three concentric cylinders - from a start point, an axis and the radii. It is a convenience for feeds and connectors: the three Object3d handles come back as a tuple so the end face of the dielectric can immediately be used for a wave port.
tools.usage:
inner, outer, diel = hfss.modeler.create_coaxial(origin, axis, inner_radius=1, outer_radius=2, diel_radius=1.8,
                                                  length=10, mat_inner="copper", mat_outer="copper", mat_diel="teflon_based")

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: [x, y, z] start of the line.

parameters.name: axis
parameters.description: Direction: 0/1/2 for X/Y/Z or the Axis enum.

parameters.name: inner_radius / diel_radius / outer_radius
parameters.description: Radii of the pin, dielectric and outer conductor (outer > diel >= inner).

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Line length along the axis.

parameters.name: mat_inner / mat_outer / mat_diel
parameters.description: Materials of the three parts.

tools.example:
from ansys.aedt.core.generic.constants import Axis
inner, outer, diel = hfss.modeler.create_coaxial([0, 0, -20], Axis.Z, inner_radius=0.635,
                                                  outer_radius=2.05, diel_radius=2.05, length=20)
port = hfss.wave_port(diel.faces[0] if diel.faces[0].center[2] < 0 else diel.faces[1], impedance=50, name="P1")
tools.notes: The outer conductor is a solid tube; in most designs set outer.solve_inside = False or replace it with a finite-conductivity boundary on the dielectric's outer face to save mesh. Radii are in model units.

tools.name: hfss.modeler.create_waveguide
tools.description: Create a standard rectangular waveguide section from its designation (WR/WG tables), returning the outer metal body and the inner vacuum box. Width and height are taken from the standard, can be parametrised with variables, and sheets can be placed on both openings for wave ports; the ideal starting point for waveguide filters, transitions and horn feeds.
tools.usage:
wg, inner = hfss.modeler.create_waveguide(origin, wg_direction_axis, wgmodel="WG0", wg_length=100, wg_thickness=None,
                                          wg_material="aluminum", parametrize_w=False, parametrize_h=False,
                                          create_sheets_on_openings=False, name=None)

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: [x, y, z] start point.

parameters.name: wg_direction_axis
parameters.description: 0/1/2 or Axis enum for the propagation axis.

parameters.name: wgmodel
parameters.description: Standard name: WG0.0, WG0, WG1 ... WG32, WG9A, WG11A, WR102 (WG numbering maps to WR sizes, e.g. WG16 = WR90).

parameters.name: wg_length / wg_thickness
parameters.description: Section length and wall thickness (default height/20).

parameters.name: parametrize_w / parametrize_h
parameters.description: Create design variables for the broad and narrow dimensions.

parameters.name: create_sheets_on_openings
parameters.description: Add port sheets at both ends.

tools.example:
from ansys.aedt.core.generic.constants import Axis
wg, air = hfss.modeler.create_waveguide([0, 0, 0], Axis.X, wgmodel="WG16", wg_length=50,
                                        create_sheets_on_openings=True, name="WR90")
sheets = [s for s in hfss.modeler.sheet_names if s.startswith("WR90")]
hfss.wave_port(sheets[0], name="P1"); hfss.wave_port(sheets[1], name="P2")
tools.notes: Dimensions come from PyAEDT's built-in table; check them against the datasheet for non-standard flanges. The outer body is solid metal; set wg.solve_inside = False or use a Perfect E on the inner faces for an ideal guide.

tools.name: hfss.modeler.create_bondwire
tools.description: Create a JEDEC-profile bond wire between a die pad and a lead-frame pad: the Draw > Bondwire tool with its loop height, pad height offset and the two profile angles. The result is a faceted swept solid, so a few bondwires are cheap while hundreds should be imported as a 3D Layout/EDB model instead.
tools.usage:
obj = hfss.modeler.create_bondwire(start, end, h1=0.2, h2=0, alpha=80, beta=5, bond_type=0,
                                   diameter=0.025, facets=6, name=None, material=None, orientation="Z", **kwargs)

parameters.name: start / end
parameters.description: [x, y, z] of the die pad and the lead pad.

parameters.name: h1
parameters.description: Loop height above the die pad.

parameters.name: h2
parameters.description: Height of the die pad above the lead frame (can be negative).

parameters.name: alpha / beta
parameters.description: Take-off angles at the die pad and at the lead in degrees.

parameters.name: bond_type
parameters.description: 0 = JEDEC 5-point, 1 = JEDEC 4-point, 2 = Low profile.

parameters.name: diameter / facets
parameters.description: Wire diameter and number of facets of the cross-section.

tools.example:
hfss.modeler.model_units = "um"
bw = hfss.modeler.create_bondwire([0, 0, 300], [800, 0, 0], h1=150, h2=300, alpha=75, beta=5,
                                  bond_type=0, diameter=25, facets=6, name="BW1", material="gold")
tools.notes: Native: oEditor.CreateBondwire(["NAME:BondwireParameters", "WireType:=", "JEDEC_5Points", "WireDiameter:=", ..., "NumSides:=", 6, "XPadPos:=", ..., "h1:=", ..., "h2:=", ..., "alpha:=", ..., "beta:=", ...], attrs). create_faceted_bondwire_from_true_surface converts an imported true-surface wire to facets.

tools.name: hfss.modeler.create_equationbased_curve
tools.description: Draw a parametric curve x(_t), y(_t), z(_t) between t_start and t_end, optionally sampled into a fixed number of straight segments and optionally given a cross-section so it becomes a sheet or solid. It is the scripted Draw > Equation Based Curve, used for log-periodic and sinuous antenna arms, tapered lines (Klopfenstein), Archimedean spirals and meander shapes that would be tedious as point lists.
tools.usage:
obj = hfss.modeler.create_equationbased_curve(x_t=0, y_t=0, z_t=0, t_start=0, t_end=1, num_points=0, name=None,
                                              xsection_type=None, xsection_orient=None, xsection_width=1,
                                              xsection_topwidth=1, xsection_height=1, xsection_num_seg=0,
                                              xsection_bend_type=None, **kwargs)

parameters.name: x_t / y_t / z_t
parameters.description: Expressions in the parameter _t (AEDT syntax, may use variables, sin/cos/exp), e.g. "_t*cos(_t)".

parameters.name: t_start / t_end
parameters.description: Parameter range.

parameters.name: num_points
parameters.description: 0 keeps an exact curve; N>0 samples N vertices (needed before some booleans).

parameters.name: xsection_type / width / height
parameters.description: "Line", "Circle", "Rectangle" or "Isosceles Trapezoid" cross-section swept along the curve.

tools.example:
arm = hfss.modeler.create_equationbased_curve(x_t="r0*exp(a*_t)*cos(_t)", y_t="r0*exp(a*_t)*sin(_t)", z_t=0,
                                              t_start=0, t_end="4*pi", num_points=400, name="SpiralArm",
                                              xsection_type="Rectangle", xsection_orient="Z",
                                              xsection_width="0.5mm", xsection_height="0.035mm")
tools.notes: Native: oEditor.CreateEquationCurve(["NAME:EquationBasedCurveParameters", "XtFunction:=", ..., "tStart:=", ..., "NumOfPointsOnCurve:=", "0", "Version:=", 1, ["NAME:PolylineXSection", ...]], attrs). Angles in the expressions are in radians unless a deg unit is written.

tools.name: PolylineSegment (Line / Arc / Spline / AngularArc) for create_polyline
tools.description: The segment_type argument of create_polyline accepts strings or PolylineSegment objects that describe how consecutive points are joined: straight lines, three-point arcs, splines through all points, or an AngularArc defined by a centre, an angle and a plane so an arc can be drawn from a single start point. Mixed lists build meander lines, rounded traces and curved transmission-line paths in one call, and the cross-section options turn the path into a sheet or a solid trace.
tools.usage:
from ansys.aedt.core.modeler.cad.polylines import PolylineSegment
seg = PolylineSegment(segment_type="AngularArc", num_seg=0, num_points=0, arc_angle=0, arc_center=None, arc_plane=None)
poly = hfss.modeler.create_polyline(points, segment_type=seg_or_list, cover_surface=False, close_surface=False, name=None,
                                    material=None, xsection_type=None, xsection_orient=None, xsection_width=1,
                                    xsection_topwidth=1, xsection_height=1, xsection_num_seg=0, xsection_bend_type=None,
                                    non_model=False)

parameters.name: segment_type
parameters.description: "Line" (2 points), "Arc" (3 points), "Spline" (all points), "AngularArc" (start point + arc_center, arc_angle, arc_plane), or a list mixing them in order.

parameters.name: arc_center / arc_angle / arc_plane
parameters.description: AngularArc definition: centre [x,y,z], signed angle with units, plane "XY"/"YZ"/"ZX".

parameters.name: num_seg
parameters.description: Segments used to discretise an arc (0 = true curve).

parameters.name: close_surface / cover_surface
parameters.description: Close the path back to the start and cover it to make a sheet.

parameters.name: xsection_bend_type
parameters.description: "Corner" (default) or "Curved" bends when a cross-section is swept.

parameters.name: Polyline object
parameters.description: Returned handle with .points, .segment_types, insert_segment(), remove_point(), set_crosssection_properties(), clone().

tools.example:
from ansys.aedt.core.modeler.cad.polylines import PolylineSegment

# straight + three-point arc + straight, as a 1 mm wide, 35 um thick trace
pts = [[0, 0, 0], [10, 0, 0], [12.5, 2.5, 0], [15, 5, 0], [15, 15, 0]]
trace = hfss.modeler.create_polyline(pts, segment_type=["Line", "Arc", "Line"], name="Trace",
                                     xsection_type="Rectangle", xsection_orient="Z",
                                     xsection_width="1mm", xsection_height="0.035mm", material="copper")

# quarter-circle arc from one start point around a centre
arc = PolylineSegment("AngularArc", arc_center=[0, 0, 0], arc_angle="90deg", arc_plane="XY")
ring = hfss.modeler.create_polyline([[5, 0, 0]], segment_type=arc, name="Arc90")
tools.notes: Native: oEditor.CreatePolyline with ["NAME:PolylineSegments", ["NAME:PLSegment", "SegmentType:=", "AngularArc", "StartIndex:=", 0, "NoOfPoints:=", 1, "NoOfSegments:=", "0", "ArcAngle:=", "90deg", "ArcCenterX:=", ...]]. Point counts must match the segment list (a 3-point arc consumes two extra points).

tools.name: hfss.modeler.create_udp / create_udm
tools.description: Instantiate a User Defined Primitive (a parametric part compiled as a DLL or written as a Python UDP under the syslib/userlib UserDefinedPrimitives folder) or a User Defined Model. AEDT ships UDPs for horns, helices, coils, RMxprt motor parts and more; scripts pass the parameter list exactly as the UDP dialog shows it and get back an Object3d whose parameters remain editable in the history tree.
tools.usage:
obj = hfss.modeler.create_udp(dll, parameters, library="syslib", name=None)
obj = hfss.modeler.create_udm(udm_full_name, parameters, library="syslib", name=None)

parameters.name: dll
parameters.description: UDP path relative to the library's UserDefinedPrimitives folder, e.g. "HFSS/Antennas/Horn" or "RMxprt/ClawPoleCore"; a .py file for Python UDPs.

parameters.name: parameters
parameters.description: List of (name, value) pairs or dicts matching the UDP's parameter names.

parameters.name: library
parameters.description: "syslib", "userlib" or "personallib".

parameters.name: udm_full_name
parameters.description: User Defined Model path for create_udm (e.g. Python or SpaceClaim models).

tools.example:
params = [{"Name": "Diameter", "Value": "10mm"}, {"Name": "Height", "Value": "30mm"},
          {"Name": "Pitch", "Value": "5mm"}, {"Name": "Turns", "Value": "6"}]
helix = hfss.modeler.create_udp("HFSS/Antennas/Helix", params, library="syslib", name="UDP_Helix")
tools.notes: Native: oEditor.CreateUserDefinedPart(["NAME:UserDefinedPrimitiveParameters", "DllName:=", "HFSS/Antennas/Helix", "Version:=", "2.0", "NoOfParameters:=", 4, "Library:=", "syslib", ["NAME:ParamVector", ["NAME:Pair", "Name:=", "Diameter", "Value:=", "10mm"], ...]], attrs). Record the GUI insertion once to get the exact parameter names of a given UDP.

tools.name: hfss.modeler.create_coordinate_system
tools.description: Create a relative coordinate system by origin plus X/Y axis vectors, by a rotation about an arbitrary axis, by a standard view, or by ZXZ/ZYZ Euler angles, referenced to Global or to another CS. Objects drawn afterwards use the working CS, and many features (Floquet lattice, near/far-field setups, anisotropic materials, SBR+ antenna placement) take a CS name, so building a CS per component is the clean way to position parts.
tools.usage:
cs = hfss.modeler.create_coordinate_system(origin=None, reference_cs="Global", name=None, mode="axis", view="iso",
                                           x_pointing=None, y_pointing=None, psi=0, theta=0, phi=0, u=None)

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: [x, y, z] in the reference CS; numbers or expression strings.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: "axis" (x_pointing/y_pointing vectors), "axisrotation" (angle theta about vector u), "view" ("iso", "XY", "XZ", "YZ"), "zxz" or "zyz" (Euler angles phi, theta, psi in degrees).

parameters.name: reference_cs
parameters.description: Parent CS name; nested systems move with their parent.

parameters.name: CoordinateSystem object
parameters.description: Returned handle with .name, .props (editable: OriginX, XAxisXvec, ...), .update(), .delete(), .change_cs_mode(), .set_as_working_cs().

tools.example:
cs1 = hfss.modeler.create_coordinate_system(origin=["x_feed", 0, "h"], name="FeedCS", mode="axis",
                                            x_pointing=[0, 1, 0], y_pointing=[0, 0, 1])
cs2 = hfss.modeler.create_coordinate_system(origin=[0, 0, 0], reference_cs="FeedCS", name="TiltCS",
                                            mode="axisrotation", u=[0, 0, 1], theta=30)
hfss.modeler.set_working_coordinate_system("TiltCS")
hfss.modeler.create_box([0, 0, 0], [5, 5, 1], name="InTiltCS")
cs2.props["OriginZ"] = "2mm"; cs2.update()
tools.notes: Native: oEditor.CreateRelativeCS(["NAME:RelativeCSParameters", "Mode:=", "Axis/Position", "OriginX:=", ..., "XAxisXvec:=", ..., "YAxisXvec:=", ...], ["NAME:Attributes", "Name:=", "FeedCS"]). The coordinate_systems property lists all CS objects; hfss.modeler.global_to_cs / reference_cs_to_global convert points.

tools.name: hfss.modeler.create_face_coordinate_system / create_object_coordinate_system
tools.description: Create coordinate systems attached to geometry rather than to fixed numbers: a face CS lives on a face with its origin and axis direction taken from that face's vertices/edges (and follows the face when parameters change), an object CS is defined from an object's topology. Both survive parametric sweeps of imported CAD, which numeric relative systems do not.
tools.usage:
fcs = hfss.modeler.create_face_coordinate_system(face, origin, axis_position, axis="X", name=None, offset=None,
                                                 rotation=0, always_move_to_end=True)
ocs = hfss.modeler.create_object_coordinate_system(assignment, origin, x_axis, y_axis, move_to_end=True, reverse_x_axis=False,
                                                   reverse_y_axis=False, name=None)

parameters.name: face
parameters.description: Face ID or FacePrimitive on which the CS is created.

parameters.name: origin / axis_position
parameters.description: Face, edge or vertex (ID or primitive) belonging to the face; origin uses its centre, axis_position defines where the X (or Y) axis points.

parameters.name: axis / rotation / offset
parameters.description: Which in-plane axis is defined, an additional rotation about the normal in degrees, and an [x, y] in-plane offset.

parameters.name: always_move_to_end
parameters.description: Keep the CS at the end of the history tree so it follows later edits of the face.

parameters.name: assignment / x_axis / y_axis
parameters.description: For object CS: the object and the entities (edges/vertices/faces) that define the axes.

tools.example:
top = hfss.modeler["Sub"].top_face_z
fcs = hfss.modeler.create_face_coordinate_system(face=top, origin=top, axis_position=top.edges[0],
                                                 axis="X", name="SubTopCS")
hfss.modeler.set_working_coordinate_system(fcs)

hfss.modeler.get_face_center(fid)
tools.notes: Native: oEditor.GetBodyNamesByPosition(["NAME:Parameters", "XPosition:=", "0mm", ...]), oEditor.GetFaceByPosition(...), oEditor.GetEdgeByPosition(...). A point exactly on a shared face returns both bodies.

tools.name: hfss.modeler.get_model_bounding_box / get_bounding_dimension / Object3d.bounding_box
tools.description: Read the extents of the whole model, or of a single object, in the global coordinate system. Scripts use them to size air regions and PMLs, to place far-field/near-field setups, to centre imported CAD, to derive the electrical size for SBR+ vs FEM decisions and to check that a scaled import came in with the expected dimensions.
tools.usage:
bb = hfss.modeler.get_model_bounding_box()        # [xmin, ymin, zmin, xmax, ymax, zmax]
dims = hfss.modeler.get_bounding_dimension()       # [dx, dy, dz]
obj.bounding_box                                   # per object
obj.bounding_dimension
hfss.modeler.get_group_bounding_box(group)

parameters.name: return
parameters.description: Floats in model units. get_model_bounding_box includes non-model objects that are visible; obounding_box gives the raw native strings.

tools.example:
xmin, ymin, zmin, xmax, ymax, zmax = hfss.modeler.get_model_bounding_box()
lam4 = 299792458 / 2.45e9 / 4 * 1000     # mm
reg = hfss.modeler.create_region([lam4]*6, pad_type="Absolute Offset")
print(hfss.modeler["Horn"].bounding_dimension)
tools.notes: Native: oEditor.GetModelBoundingBox() returns strings with units. The bounding box is axis-aligned in Global coordinates even for rotated objects; for oriented boxes use the object's vertices.

tools.name: FacePrimitive / EdgePrimitive / VertexPrimitive (obj.faces, obj.edges, obj.vertices)
tools.description: Topology handles attached to every Object3d. A FacePrimitive knows its id, center, centroid, area, normal, edges, vertices, whether it is planar, and offers is_on_bounding_box() and move_with_offset(); an EdgePrimitive has id, length, midpoint, vertices and the two adjacent faces; a VertexPrimitive has id and position. Scripts pick port faces, integration-line edges and boundary faces from these instead of hard-coded IDs, and helper properties such as obj.top_face_z / bottom_edge_x shortcut the common cases.
tools.usage:
obj = hfss.modeler["Box1"]
obj.faces / obj.edges / obj.vertices
face.id, face.center, face.area, face.normal, face.edges, face.is_planar, face.is_on_bounding_box()
edge.id, edge.length, edge.midpoint, edge.vertices, edge.segment_info
obj.top_face_z / bottom_face_z / top_face_x ... ; obj.bottom_edge_x / top_edge_y ...
obj.largest_face(n=1) / obj.smallest_face(n=1) / obj.longest_edge() / obj.shortest_edge()
hfss.modeler.get_face_by_id(id)

parameters.name: face.center
parameters.description: [x, y, z] of the face centre (planar faces) in model units.

parameters.name: face.normal
parameters.description: Outward unit normal; used to orient integration lines and lumped-port directions.

parameters.name: edge.midpoint / vertices
parameters.description: Coordinates for building integration lines between two edges.

parameters.name: top_face_z etc.
parameters.description: The face whose centre has the largest/smallest coordinate along an axis.

tools.example:
sub = hfss.modeler["Sub"]
top = sub.top_face_z
print(top.id, top.area, top.normal)
gap = hfss.modeler["FeedGap"]
line = [gap.bottom_edge_z.midpoint, gap.top_edge_z.midpoint]
hfss.lumped_port(gap.name, integration_line=line, impedance=50, name="P1")
big = hfss.modeler["Region"].largest_face()[0]
tools.notes: IDs are stable within a session but change after a re-import or history purge; keep the primitive objects, not their ints, across edits. Native queries: oEditor.GetFaceIDs(obj), GetEdgeIDsFromFace(id), GetVertexIDsFromEdge(id), GetFaceCenter(id), GetVertexPosition(id), GetEdgeLength(id), GetFaceArea(id).

tools.name: hfss.modeler.delete / delete_objects_containing / does_object_exists / cleanup_objects
tools.description: Remove objects (or groups) from the design, delete every object whose name contains a prefix, test for an object's existence, and purge PyAEDT's internal object cache of entries that no longer exist in AEDT. Deleting in a script is the usual clean-up between iterations of a generated geometry; the cache helpers matter after native oEditor calls that PyAEDT did not see.
tools.usage:
hfss.modeler.delete(assignment=None)               # None deletes everything
hfss.modeler.delete_objects_containing(contained_string, case_sensitive=True)
hfss.modeler.does_object_exists(assignment)
hfss.modeler.cleanup_objects()
hfss.modeler.refresh_all_ids()
hfss.modeler.delete_all_points()

parameters.name: assignment
parameters.description: Object name, list of names/IDs/handles or group names.

parameters.name: contained_string
parameters.description: Substring matched against object names (e.g. "tmp_").

tools.example:
if hfss.modeler.does_object_exists("tmp_sheet"):
    hfss.modeler.delete("tmp_sheet")
hfss.modeler.delete_objects_containing("scratch_")
hfss.oeditor.Delete(["NAME:Selections", "Selections:=", "OldRegion"])   # native
hfss.modeler.refresh_all_ids()   # resync after the native call
tools.notes: Deleting an object that carries boundaries deletes the boundaries too and orphans reports that reference them. hfss.modeler.delete() with no argument wipes the entire model - guard it.

tools.name: hfss.modeler.purge_history / generate_object_history
tools.description: purge_history collapses an object's history tree into a plain body (Modeler > Purge History), which speeds up regeneration of heavy boolean chains and is required before some operations on imported geometry; generate_object_history does the reverse for a 1D object, creating an editable command from an imported polyline. Purging removes parametric dependencies, so do it only on frozen geometry.
tools.usage:
hfss.modeler.purge_history(assignment, non_model=False)
hfss.modeler.generate_object_history(assignment)

parameters.name: assignment
parameters.description: Object name(s) or handles.

parameters.name: non_model
parameters.description: True converts the purged result to a non-model object.

tools.example:
hfss.modeler.import_3d_cad("C:/cad/chassis.step", healing=True)
hfss.modeler.purge_history(hfss.modeler.get_objects_in_group("Solids"))
hfss.modeler.generate_object_history("ImportedTrace")
tools.notes: Native: oEditor.PurgeHistory(["NAME:Selections", "Selections:=", "Chassis", "NewPartsModelFlag:=", "Model"]) and oEditor.GenerateHistory(["NAME:Selections", "Selections:=", "Polyline1", "NewPartsModelFlag:=", "Model", "UseCurrentCS:=", True]). Purged objects keep their material and boundaries.

tools.name: hfss.modeler.create_3dcomponent
tools.description: Save part of the design as an .a3dcomp 3D component: selected objects with their materials, boundaries, excitations, mesh operations, coordinate systems, datasets, variables and native components, optionally encrypted with a password and with hidden contents. Components are the unit of reuse for antenna elements in arrays, connectors and IP that must be shared without exposing geometry.
tools.usage:
hfss.modeler.create_3dcomponent(input_file, name=None, variables_to_include=None, assignment=None, boundaries=None,
                                excitations=None, coordinate_systems=None, reference_coordinate_system="Global",
                                is_encrypted=False, allow_edit=False, security_message="", password=None,
                                edit_password=None, password_type="UserSuppliedPassword", hide_contents=False,
                                replace_names=False, component_outline="BoundingBox", export_auxiliary=False,
                                monitor_objects=None, datasets=None, native_components=None, create_folder=True)

parameters.name: input_file
parameters.description: Output path of the .a3dcomp file.

parameters.name: assignment / boundaries / excitations / coordinate_systems / variables_to_include
parameters.description: Explicit subsets; None exports everything of that kind that belongs to the selected objects.

parameters.name: reference_coordinate_system
parameters.description: CS that becomes the component's origin on insertion.

parameters.name: is_encrypted / password / allow_edit / hide_contents
parameters.description: Encryption options: a user-supplied or internal password, whether editing is allowed with edit_password, and which objects are hidden in the target design.

parameters.name: component_outline
parameters.description: "BoundingBox" shows a box in the target when contents are hidden; None shows nothing.

parameters.name: export_auxiliary
parameters.description: Also write the auxiliary JSON with variables/definitions for PyAEDT round trips.

tools.example:
hfss.modeler.create_3dcomponent("C:/lib/patch_element.a3dcomp", name="PatchElement",
                                assignment=["Patch", "Sub", "Gnd", "FeedGap"], excitations=["P1"],
                                reference_coordinate_system="ElemCS", is_encrypted=True,
                                password="secret", hide_contents=["Patch"], component_outline="BoundingBox")
tools.notes: GUI: Draw > 3D Component Library > Create. A component with a wave port must include the port sheet and the object the sheet lies on. Lattice pairs and Floquet ports can be exported for unit-cell components used by the 3D Component Array feature.

tools.name: hfss.modeler.insert_3d_component / replace_3dcomponent / user_defined_components
tools.description: Place an .a3dcomp file into the design at a coordinate system, optionally overriding its geometry, material and design parameters and supplying the password for encrypted parts. The returned UserDefinedComponent exposes the instance's parameters, target CS, and the objects it created; replace_3dcomponent swaps an instance for another component file, and the user_defined_components dictionary lists all instances.
tools.usage:
comp = hfss.modeler.insert_3d_component(input_file, geometry_parameters=None, material_parameters="", design_parameters="",
                                        coordinate_system="Global", name=None, password=None, auxiliary_parameters=False)
hfss.modeler.replace_3dcomponent(input_file, geometry_parameters=None, ..., coordinate_system="Global", name=None, password=None)
hfss.modeler.user_defined_components          # dict name -> UserDefinedComponent
hfss.modeler.user_defined_component_names
hfss.modeler.get_3d_component_object_list(name)
hfss.flatten_3d_components(components=None, purge_history=True, password=None)

parameters.name: input_file
parameters.description: Path to the .a3dcomp.

parameters.name: geometry_parameters
parameters.description: Dict of component variable overrides, e.g. {"patch_w": "36mm"}.

parameters.name: coordinate_system
parameters.description: Target CS; the component's reference CS is aligned to it.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Required for encrypted components.

parameters.name: UserDefinedComponent
parameters.description: Handle with .name, .parameters (editable), .target_coordinate_system, .parts, .delete(), .duplicate_around_axis(), .duplicate_along_line(), .mirror(), .move(), .rotate().

tools.example:
for i in range(4):
    cs = hfss.modeler.create_coordinate_system(origin=[i * 60, 0, 0], name=f"E{i}")
    comp = hfss.modeler.insert_3d_component("C:/lib/patch_element.a3dcomp", coordinate_system=cs.name,
                                            name=f"Elem{i}", geometry_parameters={"patch_w": "37mm"})
print(hfss.modeler.user_defined_component_names)
hfss.modeler.user_defined_components["Elem0"].parameters["patch_w"] = "38mm"
tools.notes: GUI: Draw > 3D Component Library > Browse. Ports inside components become excitations named <Component>_<Port>. flatten_3d_components converts instances back to plain objects (needs the password for encrypted parts). Native: oEditor.Insert3DComponent([...]).

tools.name: hfss.modeler.import_nastran
tools.description: Import a Nastran (.nas) surface mesh - typically exported from a structural or thermal FEA tool or from a scanned model - converting its triangles into faceted HFSS objects, optionally as lightweight bodies for SBR+/HFSS Regions, with decimation to reduce triangle count, planar-face merging and grouping by part ID. Line elements can be turned into thickened wires.
tools.usage:
objects, meta = hfss.modeler.import_nastran(file_path, import_lines=True, lines_thickness=0, import_as_light_weight=False,
                                            decimation=0, group_parts=True, enable_planar_merge="True", save_only_stl=False,
                                            preview=False, merge_angle=0.001, remove_multiple_connections=False)

parameters.name: file_path
parameters.description: Path to the .nas file.

parameters.name: decimation
parameters.description: Fraction of triangles to remove (0.9 keeps 10 %) before import.

parameters.name: import_as_light_weight
parameters.description: Lightweight import for very large meshes; only valid for SBR+ and HFSS Regions.

parameters.name: enable_planar_merge
parameters.description: "True", "False" or "Auto" - merge coplanar triangles into single faces (auto disables above 50k triangles).

parameters.name: lines_thickness
parameters.description: Thicken 1D elements into wires of this radius, creating a parametric variable.

parameters.name: save_only_stl / preview
parameters.description: Write the converted STL without importing, or show a PyVista preview first.

tools.example:
objs, info = hfss.modeler.import_nastran("C:/cad/aircraft_skin.nas", decimation=0.5, enable_planar_merge="Auto",
                                          import_as_light_weight=True)
print(len(objs), info)
hfss.assign_hybrid_region([o.name for o in objs], hybrid_region="SBR+")
tools.notes: The Import Nastran extension in the Extension Manager wraps this call with a GUI. Faceted imports mesh poorly in FEM; for FEM use a STEP export from the CAD tool instead and reserve Nastran/STL for SBR+ platforms.

tools.name: hfss.modeler.import_3d_cad (options: healing, lightweight, STL reduction, units)
tools.description: The full option set of the CAD import (Modeler > Import): healing of sliver faces and gaps, importing materials from the file, creating lightweight parts for SBR+, grouping by assembly, separating disjoint bodies, importing free surfaces, STL decimation and planar merging, and forcing the input file unit when the file has none. Supports STEP, IGES, SAT/SAB, Parasolid, STL, OBJ, DXF/DWG and native formats through the licensed translators.
tools.usage:
hfss.modeler.import_3d_cad(input_file, healing=False, refresh_all_ids=True, import_materials=False, create_lightweight_part=False,
                           group_by_assembly=False, create_group=True, separate_disjoints_lumped_object=False,
                           import_free_surfaces=False, point_coincidence_tolerance=1e-06, reduce_stl=False,
                           reduce_percentage=0, reduce_error=0, merge_planar_faces=True, merge_angle=0.02, input_file_unit="Auto")

parameters.name: healing
parameters.description: Run the ACIS healer on import (fixes stitching, small faces); slower but avoids validation errors.

parameters.name: import_materials
parameters.description: Create/assign materials from the CAD file's material names when present.

parameters.name: create_lightweight_part
parameters.description: Lightweight bodies for SBR+ platforms (no history, low memory).

parameters.name: separate_disjoints_lumped_object
parameters.description: Split multi-lump bodies into separate objects.

parameters.name: reduce_stl / reduce_percentage / reduce_error
parameters.description: Triangle reduction for STL inputs.

parameters.name: input_file_unit
parameters.description: "Auto" or an explicit unit such as "mm", "in" for unit-less formats like STL.

parameters.name: refresh_all_ids
parameters.description: Rebuild the object inventory afterwards (slow on huge models; disable and call refresh_all_ids later if importing many files).

tools.example:
hfss.modeler.import_3d_cad("C:/cad/connector.step", healing=True, import_materials=True,
                           separate_disjoints_lumped_object=True)
hfss.modeler.import_3d_cad("C:/cad/radome.stl", input_file_unit="mm", reduce_stl=True, reduce_percentage=60)
print(hfss.modeler.unclassified_names)   # bodies that failed to become solids
tools.notes: Native: oEditor.Import(["NAME:NativeBodyParameters", "HealOption:=", 1, "Options:=", "-1", "FileType:=", "UnRecognized", "MaxStitchTol:=", -1, "ImportFreeSurfaces:=", False, "GroupByAssembly:=", False, "CreateGroup:=", True, "STLFileUnit:=", "mm", "MergeFacesAngle:=", 0.02, "HealSTL:=", False, "ReduceSTL:=", False, "ReducePercentage:=", 100, "PointCoincidenceTol:=", 1e-06, "CreateLightweightPart:=", False, "ImportMaterialNames:=", False, "SeparateDisjointLumps:=", False, "SourceFile:=", path]). Objects that come in as 'Unclassified' need heal_objects or a cleaner export.

tools.name: hfss.modeler.heal_objects / simplify_objects
tools.description: Repair and simplify imported geometry from a script. heal_objects exposes the Modeler > Heal dialog: auto-heal, tolerant stitching, gap tightening, removal of sliver faces, small edges/faces, holes, chamfers and blends within tolerances, and healing to solid. simplify_objects replaces complex bodies by simpler primitives (bounding boxes, cylinders) for early-stage or SBR+ models where detail is irrelevant.
tools.usage:
hfss.modeler.heal_objects(assignment, auto_heal=True, tolerant_stitch=True, simplify_geometry=True, tighten_gaps=True,
                          heal_to_solid=False, stop_after_first_stitch_error=False, max_stitch_tolerance=0.001,
                          explode_and_stitch=True, geometry_simplification_tolerance=1, maximum_generated_radius=1,
                          simplify_type=0, tighten_gaps_width=1e-05, remove_silver_faces=True, remove_small_edges=True,
                          remove_small_faces=True, silver_face_tolerance=1, small_edge_tolerance=1, small_face_area_tolerance=1,
                          bounding_box_scale_factor=0, remove_holes=True, remove_chamfers=True, remove_blends=True,
                          hole_radius_tolerance=1, chamfer_width_tolerance=1, blend_radius_tolerance=1,
                          allowable_surface_area_change=5, allowable_volume_change=5)
hfss.modeler.simplify_objects(assignment, simplify_type="Polygon Fit", extrusion_axis="Auto", clean_up=True, ...)

parameters.name: assignment
parameters.description: Comma-separated object names or list.

parameters.name: heal_to_solid
parameters.description: Try to close a stitched shell into a solid.

parameters.name: remove_holes / remove_chamfers / remove_blends + tolerances
parameters.description: Defeaturing of small cosmetic features that would otherwise dominate the mesh.

parameters.name: allowable_surface_area_change / allowable_volume_change
parameters.description: Percent limits that stop defeaturing from changing the part too much.

tools.example:
hfss.modeler.import_3d_cad("C:/cad/housing.step")
bad = hfss.modeler.unclassified_names
hfss.modeler.heal_objects(",".join(bad), heal_to_solid=True, remove_holes=True, hole_radius_tolerance=0.3)
hfss.modeler.heal_objects("Housing", auto_heal=False, remove_blends=True, blend_radius_tolerance=0.5)
tools.notes: Native: oEditor.HealObject(["NAME:Selections", "Selections:=", "Housing"], ["NAME:HealOptions", ...]). Model Resolution mesh operations are the solver-side alternative to geometric defeaturing and do not alter the CAD.

tools.name: hfss.export_3d_model / hfss.modeler.export_3d_model
tools.description: Write the model, or a subset of objects, to a neutral CAD file (STEP by default; IGES, SAT/SAB, Parasolid, STL, OBJ) with optional format version. Used to hand HFSS geometry to mechanical CAD, to Icepak/Mechanical, to SBR+ as lightweight parts, or to archive a generated model outside the .aedt.
tools.usage:
hfss.export_3d_model(file_name="", file_path="", file_format=".step", assignment_to_export=None,
                     assignment_to_remove=None, major_version=-1, minor_version=-1)

parameters.name: file_name / file_path
parameters.description: Name without extension and target folder (working directory by default).

parameters.name: file_format
parameters.description: ".step", ".igs", ".sat", ".sab", ".x_t", ".stl", ".obj".

parameters.name: assignment_to_export / assignment_to_remove
parameters.description: Include only these objects, or everything except these.

parameters.name: major_version / minor_version
parameters.description: Format version (e.g. SAT 25.0); -1 uses the default.

tools.example:
hfss.export_3d_model(file_name="antenna_no_air", file_path="C:/work/cad", file_format=".step",
                     assignment_to_remove=["Region", "PML1"])
tools.notes: Native: oEditor.Export(["NAME:ExportParameters", "AllowRegionDependentPartSelectionForPMLCreation:=", True, "AllowRegionSelectionForPMLCreation:=", True, "Selections:=", "Patch,Sub", "File Name:=", "C:/work/cad/antenna.step", "Major Version:=", -1, "Minor Version:=", -1]). Sheets export as surfaces; encrypted 3D component contents are not exported.

tools.name: hfss.modeler.model_units / hfss.modeler.rescale_model / hfss.units
tools.description: Read or set the modeler length unit for the design (Modeler > Units). Assigning a new unit either re-labels the existing coordinates (default) or rescales the geometry so its physical size is preserved, depending on rescale_model. Plain numbers passed to any create_* call are interpreted in this unit, so scripts normally set it first; hfss.units exposes the default units PyAEDT uses for frequency, time, angle and length.
tools.usage:
hfss.modeler.model_units            # 'mm'
hfss.modeler.model_units = "um"      # change unit
hfss.modeler.rescale_model = True    # rescale geometry on the next unit change
hfss.units.length / hfss.units.frequency / hfss.units.angle

parameters.name: rescale_model
parameters.description: False (default) keeps the numbers and changes their meaning; True multiplies coordinates so the model keeps its physical size.

tools.example:
hfss.modeler.model_units = "mil"      # PCB design in mils
trace = hfss.modeler.create_box([0, 0, 0], [500, 10, 1.4], name="Trace")   # 500 mil long
print(hfss.modeler.model_units, hfss.units.length)
tools.notes: Native: oEditor.SetModelUnits(["NAME:Units Parameter", "Units:=", "mil", "Rescale:=", False]). Variables keep their own units regardless of the model unit; only unit-less numbers are affected.

tools.name: hfss.modeler.create_sheet_to_ground / create_plane / create_point / fit_all
tools.description: Small helpers used around ports and views: create_sheet_to_ground builds a vertical sheet from an object's face down to a ground object (the classic lumped-port feed sheet), create_plane adds a reference plane object for sectioning and field plots, create_point places a point for near-field probing or as a Fields Calculator point, and fit_all zooms the view (useful before export_model_picture).
tools.usage:
sheet = hfss.modeler.create_sheet_to_ground(assignment, ground_name=None, axisdir=0, sheet_dim=1)
plane = hfss.modeler.create_plane(name=None, plane_base_x="0mm", plane_base_y="0mm", plane_base_z="0mm",
                                  plane_normal_x="0mm", plane_normal_y="0mm", plane_normal_z="1mm", color="(143 175 143)")
pt = hfss.modeler.create_point(position, name=None, color="(143 175 143)")
hfss.modeler.fit_all()

parameters.name: assignment / ground_name
parameters.description: Signal object and ground object; None uses the closest face of a PEC/conductor below.

parameters.name: axisdir
parameters.description: Direction from the object towards ground (hfss.AxisDir.ZNeg etc. or 0-5).

parameters.name: sheet_dim
parameters.description: Width of the generated sheet in model units.

parameters.name: plane_base_* / plane_normal_*
parameters.description: Point and normal defining the plane object.

tools.example:
feed = hfss.modeler.create_sheet_to_ground("Patch", ground_name="Gnd", axisdir=hfss.AxisDir.ZNeg, sheet_dim=2)
hfss.lumped_port(feed.name, integration_line=hfss.AxisDir.ZNeg, impedance=50, name="P1")
cut = hfss.modeler.create_plane("CutYZ", plane_normal_x="1mm", plane_normal_y="0mm", plane_normal_z="0mm")
hfss.post.create_fieldplot_cutplane(cut.name, "Mag_E", plot_name="E_cut")
hfss.modeler.fit_all()
tools.notes: Plane objects are non-model and appear under Planes in the tree; the built-in Global:XY/YZ/XZ planes can be used by name for cut-plane plots. Native: oEditor.FitAll().
